summary.text: In Pausanias' closing Theban king-list, Ptolemy is the son of Damasichthon and the father of Xanthus — the penultimate generation before sole kingship ended at seven-gated Thebes.
Not to be confused with the many other bearers of the name in Greek myth and history; this Ptolemy belongs only to Pausanias' brief Peneleid roll after Autesion's departure.

story.text: Pausanias names him in a single genealogical clause: Damasichthon had a son Ptolemy, who was the father of Xanthus. He stands between the king chosen when Autesion migrated to the Dorians and the last sole ruler whose death by treachery in a duel persuaded the Thebans to divide their government.
